chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us about this, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Tamim ibn Buhlool narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Zayd narrated to us, from his father, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father Al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said:
Nine-tenths of the sustenance is in commerce, and the remaining part is in the spoils of war (sabiyah), meaning the sheep.
ai.seo_question: What are the primary sources of sustenance according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq attributes this narration to the Prophet via the Imams, emphasizing that commercial trade constitutes the primary source of sustenance (nine-tenths), while the remaining tenth is derived from *sabai* (spoils of war), specifically illustrated by livestock. This distinction underscores the Prophetic endorsement of active economic participation and trade as a legitimate and preferred means of livelihood within the Shia tradition, contrasting it with the more limited scope of war booty.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-46 A similar account was narrated by Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Qat’tan who narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakaria al-Qat’tan quoted Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Tamim ibn Buhlool, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abdul Rahman al-Makhzoomi, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Zayd, on the authority of his father Zayd ibn Ali, on the authority of his father Ali ibn al-Hussein (MGB), on the authority of his father Al-Hussein ibn Ali (MGB), on the authority of his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,
“Nine-tenths of the daily bread is in commerce and last tenth is in the skin - that is the skin of sheep.”
